sections.title: Lesson 4.1: Investment Company Act of 1940
sections.overview: The Investment Company Act of 1940 classifies investment companies into three categories: Face-Amount Certificate (FAC) companies, Unit Investment Trusts (UITs), and Management Investment Companies (open-end and closed-end). This lesson covers their structural differences, mutual fund share classes, pricing mechanics (NAV/POP), sales charge rules, breakpoints, prospectus delivery, and Subchapter M conduit taxation.
key_concepts: Investment company: pools investor money to invest based on a stated objective; provides diversification and professional management.
Three classes under '40 Act: (1) FACs, (2) UITs, (3) Management Companies (open-end and closed-end).
FAC: contract guaranteeing payment of a stated face amount at a future date in exchange for lump-sum or periodic payments; few exist today.

UIT: organized under a trust indenture; trustees (no BOD); no active management; sells redeemable units representing undivided interest in a fixed portfolio; terminates at bond maturity or arbitrary date for equity UITs.
Management companies: actively managed; either open-end (mutual fund) or closed-end (publicly traded fund).
Closed-end fund: fixed share offering via IPO; trades on exchange/OTC at market price (premium/discount to NAV); may issue common, preferred, and debt.
Open-end fund (mutual fund): continuous primary offering; issues only common stock; redeems shares directly at NAV; sold in full or fractional shares.
Forward pricing: orders entered before 4:00 pm ET receive that day's next-computed NAV/POP; later orders receive next business day's price.
Mutual fund share classes: Class A (front-end load), Class B (back-end load/CDSC, converts to A), Class C (level load, ~1% 12b-1), No-load (sold at NAV).
Class A best for large investments + long horizon (breakpoints); Class B best for small + long; Class C best for short horizons (1–5 years).
Breakpoints: quantity discounts on Class A shares only; available to individuals, spouses, minor children, corporations — NOT investment clubs.
Letter of Intent (LOI): allows reduced sales charge if investor commits to reach breakpoint within 13 months; may be backdated up to 90 days; binding on fund only; shares held in escrow.
Rights of accumulation: reduced sales charges on subsequent purchases based on greater of current NAV or total purchases; no time limit.
Combination privilege: combine investments across funds in same family to reach breakpoint.
Exchange/conversion privilege: switch between funds in same family without new sales charge; still a taxable event.
NAV calculated at least once per business day, typically at 4:00 pm ET close.
Expense ratio: fund expenses / average net assets; excludes sales charges/loads; includes manager fee, admin fees, BOD costs, 12b-1 fees. Typical stock funds: 1–1.5%; bond funds: 0.5–1%.
Maximum sales charge on mutual funds: 8.5% of POP (Investment Company Act of 1940).
Mutual fund dividend dates: Declaration → Record/Payable → Ex-Date (ex-date set by BOD, day AFTER record date — because trades settle same-day with the fund).

Disclosure documents: Statutory (full) prospectus, Summary prospectus (Rule 498), Statement of Additional Information (SAI — delivered within 3 business days of request), Omitting prospectus (Rule 482 — advertisement/tombstone).
Prospectus performance disclosure: 1-, 5-, and 10-year (or life of fund if shorter).
Prospectuses may NEVER be altered, highlighted, or marked up.
Subchapter M (conduit/pipeline tax theory): fund must distribute at least 90% of net investment income (NII) to avoid taxation on distributed amount; fund still pays tax on retained portion.
Breakpoint sale violation: failing to inform customer of an upcoming breakpoint that would reduce sales charges; the failure to disclose — not the order itself — is the violation.
Variable annuity subaccounts are organized as either UITs (indirectly managed) or open-end management companies (directly managed).

TAILORED SHAREHOLDER REPORTS (UPDATED): Open-end funds (mutual funds and ETFs) must deliver concise Tailored Shareholder Reports (TSRs) to retail shareholders; SEC Rule 30e-3 was rescinded for open-end funds. Compliance date 7/24/2024 (SEC Rel. 33-11125).

MONEY MARKET FUND REFORM 2023 (UPDATED — Rule 2a-7): Redemption gates ELIMINATED. Minimum daily liquid assets raised to 25%; weekly liquid assets raised to 50%. MANDATORY liquidity fee imposed on institutional prime/tax-exempt funds when daily net redemptions exceed 5% of NAV. Discretionary liquidity fee up to 2% remains available for non-government MMFs at board discretion. Mandatory fee compliance: 10/2/2024 (SEC Rel. IC-34959).
rules: Investment Company Act of 1940 — classifies investment companies; governs registration, operations, sales practices.
Securities Act of 1933 — investment company shares must be registered; prospectus delivery required.
Investment Company Act Section 3(a) — definition of investment company.
Section 4 — classification (FAC, UIT, management).
Section 5 — subclassification of management companies (open vs. closed; diversified vs. nondiversified).
Rule 12b-1 — permits open-end funds to charge distribution fees from fund assets.
Rule 498 — Summary Prospectus requirements (cover legend, ticker, toll-free number/website, mandated sequence).
Rule 482 — Omitting prospectus (advertisements/tombstones).
Rule 462 — referenced for omitting prospectus context.
Subchapter M of Internal Revenue Code — conduit tax treatment requires ≥90% NII distribution.
FINRA Rule 2342 — breakpoint sales; disclosure of breakpoint schedules required.
SEC Rel. 33-11125 (effective 7/24/2024) — Tailored Shareholder Reports required; Rule 30e-3 rescinded for open-end funds.

SEC Rel. IC-34959 (compliance 10/2/2024) — Rule 2a-7 reforms: mandatory liquidity fee on institutional prime/tax-exempt MMFs when daily net redemptions >5%; gates eliminated; daily liquid assets 25%, weekly liquid assets 50%.
Diversified company (75-5-10 rule under '40 Act): 75% of assets — no more than 5% in any one issuer, no more than 10% of issuer's voting securities.
formulas: Net Assets = Total Assets - Total Liabilities
NAV per Share = Net Assets / Shares Outstanding
Expense Ratio = Fund Expenses / Average Net Assets
Subchapter M minimum distribution = 90% of Net Investment Income
Shares Purchased = Amount Invested / POP per Share (open-end, fractional allowed)
mnemonics: DERP (stocks) vs. DR-Ex (mutual funds): Declaration → Record/Payable → Ex-date for funds (ex comes AFTER record).
FUM — three '40 Act companies: Face-amount certificates, Unit investment trusts, Management companies.
ABC of share classes: A = front-load (Affordable for big/long), B = Back-end (CDSC), C = Continuous level load (short-term).

sections.title: Lesson 4.2: Life Insurance-Based Products (Variable Annuities)
sections.overview: Variable annuities are insurance contracts that combine a tax-deferred investment vehicle (the separate account) with a mortality guarantee (lifetime income). Because the investor bears the investment risk, VAs are securities and require both insurance and securities licenses to sell. This lesson covers VA structure, annuitization, taxation, 1035 exchanges, and suitability standards under FINRA Rule 2330.
key_concepts: Annuity: insurance contract providing a stream of payments — for life, until a certain age, or for a fixed period — backed by a mortality guarantee.
Fixed annuity: insurance company bears investment risk; promises a stated rate; NOT a security.
Variable annuity: investor bears investment risk; premiums invested in the separate account; IS a security (requires Series 6/7 + state insurance license).
Separate account: holds subaccounts (function like mutual fund portfolios) with various objectives (growth, income, etc.).
Directly managed separate account → registered as open-end management company; indirectly managed → registered as UIT.
Death benefit (accumulation phase): beneficiary receives greater of total contributions or current account value if owner dies before annuitization.
No annual contribution limit on nonqualified VAs; qualified VAs (e.g., inside 403(b)/401(k)) follow plan limits.
Annuitization: one-time, IRREVERSIBLE election; owner surrenders lump-sum ownership in exchange for guaranteed lifetime income stream.
Payout calculation factors — SAAPI: Sex, Age, Account amount, Payout option, assumed Interest rate (AIR). Inflation is NOT a factor.
AIR (Assumed Interest Rate): benchmark for variable payout; if actual separate account performance > AIR, next payment increases; if < AIR, decreases; if = AIR, unchanged.
Accumulation units (during pay-in) → Annuity units (fixed number after annuitization; value fluctuates).
Tax deferral: growth in separate account not taxed until withdrawal; withdrawals taxed as ORDINARY income (not capital gains).
Random/lump-sum withdrawals: LIFO — growth (taxable) comes out first; then principal (return of cost basis, nontaxable).
Annuitized payments: portion is return of principal (exclusion ratio, nontaxable) and portion is ordinary income.
10% IRS penalty on taxable portion if withdrawn before age 59½ (same as IRA).
1035 Exchange: tax-free transfer from one annuity to another (or life-to-annuity); surrender charges may still apply.

VA SUITABILITY (FINRA Rule 2330): VAs are SUPPLEMENTAL retirement vehicles, NOT primary; not suitable if customer needs liquidity, has low risk tolerance, dislikes equity markets, or would fund via cashing out existing insurance/annuity, home refinance, or home equity.
Max other tax-advantaged retirement accounts (IRA, 401(k)) before recommending a VA.
Generally NOT suitable inside an IRA (redundant tax deferral) absent specific other benefits.
Costs disclosed: mortality & expense (M&E), administrative fees, investment advisory/management fees, custodial fees, surrender charges.
Surrender charges typically decline over 5–8 years (similar to Class B mutual fund CDSC).
VA PROSPECTUS DELIVERY (UPDATED): Issuers may deliver an Initial Summary Prospectus (ISP) with the full statutory prospectus available online or on request. Effective 7/1/2020 (SEC Rel. 33-10765).
Variable life insurance is also a security but is NOT tested on the SIE.
rules: FINRA Rule 2330 — Members' Responsibilities Regarding Deferred Variable Annuities; supervisory and suitability review required; principal review within 7 business days of customer signing.
Investment Company Act of 1940 — separate accounts must be registered as UIT or open-end management company.
Securities Act of 1933 — variable contracts must be registered; prospectus delivery required.
IRC Section 1035 — tax-free exchange between like insurance/annuity contracts.
IRC Section 72 — taxation of annuity distributions; 10% penalty before 59½ on taxable portion.
SEC Rel. 33-10765 (effective 7/1/2020) — Initial Summary Prospectus permitted for variable contracts.
formulas: Exclusion Ratio = Investment in Contract / Expected Return (portion of each annuity payment treated as nontaxable return of principal)
Random withdrawal taxation (LIFO): Taxable Amount = Withdrawal up to amount of accumulated growth; remainder = nontaxable principal
Payout direction (variable annuity): If separate account return > AIR → payment ↑; if < AIR → payment ↓; if = AIR → unchanged
mnemonics: SAAPI — payout calculation: Sex, Age, Account amount, Payout option, Interest rate (AIR). NO inflation.
LIFO for VA withdrawals — Last In (gains) First Out (taxed first).
1035 = tax-free annuity-to-annuity exchange (surrender charges still apply).
VAs are SUPPLEMENTAL — max out qualified plans first.
